closed_world.value: Las Vegas and surrounding desert; narrator arrives from Oakland and checks into Motel 6 near Chinatown
closed_world.quote: I checked into the Motel 6 near Chinatown and fell asleep with my shoes on and my gun still strapped to my ankle.

investigator.value: First-person narrator, armed investigator or detective arriving in Las Vegas from Oakland
investigator.quote: my gun still strapped to my ankle. I slept stupid for nine hours straight and woke up at six in the morning

red_herring.value: The beam of light from the pyramid casino is mistaken for a UFO, establishing a motif of misreading evidence — potentially seeding the reader to distrust first impressions.
red_herring.quote: I thought the cloud was a UFO or something and nearly hit the truck ahead of me.

clue_fairness.value: The narrator's gun strapped to ankle and badge are disclosed to the reader in passing, establishing investigator identity and arming details available to reader from the outset.
clue_fairness.quote: my gun still strapped to my ankle

social_world.value: A transactional, low-trust urban underclass world: cash overrides authority (badge vs. money at motel desk), ethnic insularity, immigrant service economy in Las Vegas Chinatown fringe.
social_world.quote: I thought about flashing him my badge, but instead I brandished three days' stay in advance, cash

media_and_audience.value: Las Vegas's mythology (UFO-like beam visible from space, neon spectacle) frames how events are perceived and misread — the city's public image actively distorts witness perception.
media_and_audience.quote: you can even see the beam from space... My disappointment surprised me.

investigator_wound.value: Investigator is an outsider (Oakland origin, first time in Vegas), sleep-deprived, physically depleted, and prone to misperception — vulnerability established as cognitive and sensory unreliability.
investigator_wound.quote: My tired pulpy brain at the time, I thought the cloud was a UFO or something and nearly hit the truck ahead of me.
